subject.title: fix(memory): exclude extraPaths from shared scope hash to avoid unnecessary reindexing

question: Should same-workspace memory-source agents share one default SQLite index when their extraPaths and session-indexing scopes can differ, and what migration/filter contract is required before that becomes the default?
rationale: The correct answer changes persistent storage identity and agent/session visibility boundaries, so automation cannot safely choose between sharing by workspace, sharing by full source set, or keeping session/extraPath scopes agent-local.

options.title: Redesign before merge
options.body: Require path/ref ownership, session visibility enforcement across CLI and tool paths, and a doctor migration or rebuild-warning path before changing the default DB identity.

options.title: Accept workspace as boundary
options.body: Maintainers can explicitly accept same-workspace sharing, but the PR must document and test the privacy, migration, and extraPaths deletion semantics as intentional behavior.

options.title: Pause this branch
options.body: Keep https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/95724 canonical and close or replace this PR if the storage contract is not ready.

recommendation.title: Redesign before merge
recommendation.body: Require path/ref ownership, session visibility enforcement across CLI and tool paths, and a doctor migration or rebuild-warning path before changing the default DB identity.

likelyOwner.reason: The current per-agent SQLite memory-store path and recent memory-host SDK facade cleanup are in vincentkoc's recent history.
